macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks end sharply higher as AI optimism returns
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 1.49%, the Dow gained 0.71%, and the Nasdaq jumped 2.26% to a record high, with gains led by AI-related names such as AMD. Reuters said the rally was supported by lower Treasury yields and weaker oil prices.

items.title: Fed officials keep a hawkish tone on inflation
items.summary: St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said further rate increases may still be needed to contain persistent inflation, reinforcing expectations that the Fed is not done tightening. Market coverage also noted traders pricing in a meaningful chance of another hike at the next FOMC meeting.

items.title: Bank of Canada warns new U.S. tariffs could slow growth
items.summary: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said new U.S. tariffs could slash Canada’s fourth-quarter growth to below 1%, highlighting fresh downside risks for investment and hiring. The comment adds to the day’s central-bank focus as markets assess growth and inflation tradeoffs.

items.title: AMD and other chip stocks surge on AI demand
items.summary: AMD shares rallied strongly and pushed its market value above $1 trillion, while other semiconductor names such as Arm and Intel also posted big gains. The move helped drive the Nasdaq’s outperformance and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index’s sharp advance.

items.title: Oil prices slide, helping risk assets
items.summary: U.S. crude and Brent fell sharply as markets speculated about progress in Middle East talks at the UN, easing pressure on equities and Treasury yields. Lower energy prices were cited as a key reason for the broader rally in stocks.

items.title: Markets start the day with softer dollar and firmer futures
items.summary: Live market coverage showed the dollar slightly softer, while U.S. equity futures pointed higher as risk appetite improved. The tone was consistent with the prior session’s strong close in U.S. equities.

items.title: European stocks and U.S. futures lifted by global risk appetite
items.summary: Overnight reporting said European equities rose alongside U.S. stock futures, with optimism tied to falling oil prices and the possibility of progress in U.S.-China relations. Semiconductor strength remained a central theme in the global move higher.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin tops $87,000, triggering broad crypto rally and heavy short liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin surged past $87,000 for the first time since January, with Ethereum, XRP, and Dogecoin also rising sharply. More than $1 billion in crypto positions were liquidated over the last 24 hours, mostly bearish shorts, as market sentiment flipped to extreme greed.

items.title: Bitcoin extends rebound above $87,000 as traders cite ETF flows and risk appetite
items.summary: Multiple market reports say Bitcoin briefly moved above $87,000, extending a sharp rebound that also lifted major altcoins. The move came alongside stronger ETF-related flows and a broader Wall Street risk rally.

items.title: Altcoins lead the day as Bitcoin plays catch-up after SEC and CFTC developments
items.summary: Crypto markets saw strong gains across several large caps and high-beta altcoins, with NEAR, Avalanche, and The Graph among the top performers in one 24-hour window. The report linked the rally to recent U.S. regulatory momentum, including SEC approval of limited tokenized-share trading and draft CFTC rules sent to the White House.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum rally as short liquidations wipe out leveraged bets
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed above $85,000 to $87,000 across several market reports, while Ethereum also advanced strongly. CoinGlass-based reporting cited roughly $750 million to more than $1 billion in liquidations over 24 hours, with the majority coming from short positions.

items.title: SEC tokenization move lifts Ethereum-linked stocks and crypto sentiment
items.summary: A market report said Ethereum rose after the SEC opened a regulated path for tokenized U.S. stocks, which also boosted related equities such as Bitmine and Coinbase. The development was framed as a notable project and market-structure shift for blockchain-based financial products.

items.title: Bitcoin reaches highest level since January as crypto winter debate intensifies
items.summary: Another market report said Bitcoin traded near $85,000 after reaching its strongest level since January, with traders watching whether the move confirms the end of the crypto winter. The report pointed to ETF-holder cost basis levels as a closely watched threshold.

items.title: BTC, ETH and altcoins extend gains; BNB and DOGE also strengthen
items.summary: Market snapshots showed Bitcoin and Ethereum both higher over 24 hours, with BNB and Dogecoin among the major gainers in a broad rebound. One report also highlighted Bittensor as an outsized performer among large-cap tokens.

items.title: DOGE and XRP post double-digit gains as broader crypto market rebounds
items.summary: A market roundup said Bitcoin's move above $87,000 helped drive a wider altcoin surge, with Dogecoin and XRP logging double-digit gains in some sessions. The piece framed the move as part of a broad recovery across major crypto assets.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Bungie says it will restore vaulted Destiny 2 content and rework Marathon
items.summary: Bungie outlined plans to bring back removed Destiny 2 content and make substantial changes to Marathon as it tries to rebuild player trust after recent criticism. The update is one of the biggest live-service game development stories in the last day.

items.title: Blizzard reportedly reveals a StarCraft open-world shooter targeting 2030
items.summary: A new report says Blizzard has unveiled an open-world StarCraft shooter with a launch target around 2030. If confirmed, it would mark a major expansion of the franchise beyond its traditional RTS roots.

items.title: Xbox event showcases 17 games, including Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and Fallout 76 update
items.summary: Microsoft’s latest showcase featured a trailer for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, a new Fallout 76 content update, and fresh footage from multiple upcoming titles. The event also included reveals tied to Persona 4 Revival, Raji: Kaliyuga, Wo Long 2, and Bloodstained: The Scarlet Engagement.

items.title: WarDogs early-access trailer and upcoming console release draw attention
items.summary: WarDogs is getting a Steam early-access launch, with a launch trailer highlighting its large-scale military FPS action. The game is also slated to arrive on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S in 2028.

items.title: Heart Machine faces layoffs and possible closure
items.summary: Reports say Hyper Light Drifter developer Heart Machine has laid off a majority of its staff and may be at risk of closing. The news is a significant industry development for an influential indie studio.

items.title: Marvel’s Wolverine sales momentum continues
items.summary: A report says Marvel’s Wolverine sold 1.9 million copies in its first three days, generating about $130 million in revenue for PlayStation 5. The strong opening makes it one of the most notable recent game release stories.

items.title: Dune: Awakening is listed as a new release
items.summary: Game Informer’s release listings include Dune: Awakening among the notable new titles. The appearance suggests fresh release activity across the PC/console market.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Google hit with €403 million GDPR fine over location data handling
items.summary: Ireland’s data protection watchdog fined Google €403 million for breaching EU privacy rules by mishandling users’ location data. The case is one of the biggest tech-regulatory actions reported in the last day.

items.title: Huawei launches new chip technologies in challenge to Nvidia
items.summary: Huawei unveiled new chip technologies as it continues to compete with leading global semiconductor firms. The launch underscores intensifying pressure on the AI-chip supply chain and broader chip market.

items.title: Gates Foundation convenes 60-organization coalition on language access tools
items.summary: The Gates Foundation assembled a coalition including Anthropic, Google and the OpenAI Foundation to expand language diversity in digital tools. The effort focuses on underrepresented languages and global accessibility.

items.title: Robotic boat crosses the Atlantic unaided
items.summary: A robotic boat completed an unaided Atlantic crossing, marking a notable development in autonomous marine systems. The feat highlights continued progress in long-distance unmanned navigation.

items.title: Meta’s Muse app drives a surge in consumer product interest
items.summary: Meta’s Muse app has drawn strong consumer attention, including rapid download growth and a sharp move in Meta shares. The development is part of a broader rebound in tech stocks tied to product and platform momentum.
